info.name: Ecommerce Store MS — Mobile API
info.description:
End-to-end collection for every endpoint under /api/v1/mobile, generated from docs/MOBILE_API.md and docs/CUSTOMER_WALLET_API.md (the authoritative, code-verified reference for this API as of 2026-09-02).

## Setup
1. Set the `base_url` collection variable (default `http://localhost:3000`).
2. Run **Authentication > Login (Customer)** (or **Verify OTP**) — the `token` variable is saved automatically from the response.
3. For the Agent folder, run **Authentication > Login (Agent / Sub-agent)** to populate `agent_token`; for Delivery Person, run **Login (Delivery Person)** to populate `delivery_token`.
4. Fill in resource-id variables (`product_id`, `booking_id`, `category_id`, `subscription_id`, `order_id`, `banner_id`, `task_id`, `pincode`) as you create/observe real records, or override them per-request.

## Known API quirks worth testing against (see docs for details)
- Several delivery-check endpoints return **HTTP 200 even when the result is 'not deliverable'** — always check the `data` payload, not just the status code.
- `POST /agent/customers` and `POST /agent/leads` use `{status, message, data}`, not `{success, message, data}` like almost everything else.
- `POST /delivery/bulk_update` with `status: "failed"` currently 500s and aborts the whole batch (invalid enum value server-side) — avoid it until fixed.
- Wallet payment (`booking[use_wallet]`) is documented separately in CUSTOMER_WALLET_API.md and lives on `POST ecommerce/bookings`, not its own endpoint.

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Login, registration, password recovery, and OTP login. None of these endpoints require an Authorization header.

request.description: Tries User, Customer, DeliveryPerson, then SubAgent tables in order. Response shape (and which role-specific fields appear) depends on which account type matched. Auto-saves `token`/`customer_id` on success.
Same endpoint as customer login — the account type is resolved server-side. Note: a direct SubAgent-table match does NOT check password at all (see docs). Auto-saves `agent_token` on success.
Same endpoint; matches the DeliveryPerson table. Auto-saves `delivery_token` on success.
Creates a Customer + paired User row. Does NOT return a JWT — call POST /auth/login afterward.
Creates a User with status:false (pending admin approval) — cannot log in until an admin activates the account.
Sends a password-reset email to a Customer account (case-insensitive email match). Reset token is valid 24 hours.
Completes the reset using the token from the email link.
Sends a 6-digit SMS OTP (MSG91), valid 5 minutes, 60s resend cooldown, max 5 requests/hour. Gated by SystemSetting.otp_login_enabled?.
Verifies the OTP and logs in (creating a minimal User+Customer pair on first-ever login for that mobile). Auto-saves `token`/`customer_id` on success.

item.name: E-commerce - Catalog & Search
item.description: Category/product browsing, search, filters, and ecommerce banners. Only products/banners/featured_products are public — everything else here needs a customer bearer token.

request.description: Returns all active categories. Cached.
404 if category not found.
Paginated product listing scoped to one category (active + available_for_sale only).
PUBLIC — no auth required. Paginated, filterable, cached product listing.
Auth required (despite the list endpoint being public). Includes related_products, reviews, and a static delivery_info placeholder — use check_delivery for a real answer.
PUBLIC. Despite the name, this is simply the newest products, not a curated flag.
One of query/q/search is required — 400 if all are absent.
Returns filter facets (categories, price_range, brands, sort_options) for building the product listing UI. Cached.
PUBLIC. Distinct from the standalone /banners module below — same underlying model, different response shape. Cached per location.

item.name: E-commerce - Delivery Validation & Location
item.description: Three independent delivery-checking mechanisms (product DeliveryRule, global DeliveryCharge, external India Post pincode API) — see each request's description for which one it uses.

request.description: Per-product DeliveryRule check. IMPORTANT: HTTP 200 + success:true even when NOT deliverable — check data.deliverable, not the top-level success flag.
Global DeliveryCharge table lookup (not tied to any product). Also returns 200 + success:true for a non-deliverable pincode — check data.deliverable.
Validates against the external api.postalpincode.in service (cached). Returns HTTP 200 even when data.valid is false — check the payload, not the status code.
Validates pincode via India Post, then checks stock + DeliveryRule per product id. success mirrors overall_delivery_available; still HTTP 200 on failure.
Global DeliveryCharge lookup. Unlike the other delivery endpoints, this one DOES use a real 422 for an unserviceable/invalid pincode.
Updates the authenticated customer's stored lat/long. Note: pincode is echoed back only — Customer has no pincode column, it is not actually persisted.
Customer resolved by email from the JWT. Includes statistics + last-5 recent orders/bookings in basic form.
All fields optional; accepted top-level, or nested under `customer`/`ecommerce` (checked in that order). Cannot change email/id.

item.name: E-commerce - Bookings & Checkout
item.description: Two separate order-placement flows with different payment models — see request descriptions.

request.description: Validates every product exists first (422 with unavailable_products if not) but allows booking past available stock. Set booking[use_wallet]=true to pay from the customer wallet first — see CUSTOMER_WALLET_API.md.
Customer resolved by email from JWT. Ordered most-recent-first.
Lightweight polling endpoint for Cashfree payment status on one booking.
payment_method 'cod' confirms immediately; any other value opens a Cashfree payment session (booking created as 'draft'). use_wallet is NOT supported on this endpoint.
Queries Cashfree directly and updates the booking if paid. Can return HTTP 200 with success:false when payment isn't complete yet — check the body, not just the status.

item.name: E-commerce - Orders
item.description: Order records (distinct from Booking) for the authenticated customer.

request.description: Order (distinct from Booking) records for the authenticated customer.
Scoped to customer.orders; 404 if not owned by this customer.

item.name: E-commerce - Subscriptions
item.description: Recurring milk-delivery subscriptions (MilkSubscription model, despite the generic route name).

request.description: Recurring milk-delivery subscription (despite the generic route name, this is always MilkSubscription). pincode is validated via the external India Post API — request fails if unserviceable. Creating this synchronously generates one MilkDeliveryTask per delivery date in range.
Includes the 10 most recent delivery tasks.
Only succeeds from status 'active'. Does NOT bulk-update already-generated delivery tasks.
Only succeeds from status 'paused'.
Succeeds from any status except already-'cancelled'.

Balance + paginated transaction history. Lazily creates a zero-balance wallet on first call. 403 if SystemSetting.customer_wallet_enabled? is false. See docs/CUSTOMER_WALLET_API.md — wallet payment itself happens via POST ecommerce/bookings with booking[use_wallet]=true, not a separate endpoint.

item.name: Customer Portfolio
item.description: Insurance policy list + installment/renewal reminders (Life + Motor).

request.description: All of the customer's Life + Motor insurance policies plus summary counts. Customer-role tokens only — an agent/sub_agent token 500s here (see docs).
Upcoming premium installments (next 60 days) for Life + Motor policies, plus renewal-style installments for policies expired within the last 18 months.
Policies renewing within 2 months across Life, Motor, Travel, General, Other (each only if its model is present).

item.name: Settings
item.description: Profile, password, terms, contact, and helpdesk — shared across roles.

request.description: Field set depends on the authenticated user's type (Customer/User-agent/SubAgent). Works with customer, agent, or sub_agent tokens.
Permitted params depend on user type — see docs. Params are top-level, not nested.
Behavior differs by resolved user type (Customer routes through its linked User; SubAgent/User change their own password_digest).
Response shape depends on caller role (Customer vs. User/SubAgent).
Creates a ClientRequest ticket. priority is always 'medium', not client-settable.

item.name: Banners
item.description: Standalone banner module — all 4 endpoints are public, no auth required.

request.description: PUBLIC. All currently-active banners, cached. No filtering params are actually read.
PUBLIC. Valid display_location enum values for a location picker.
PUBLIC. 404 if the banner is inactive OR outside its display date window.
PUBLIC. Logs the click (no counter persisted) and returns the redirect_link. Only checks Banner.active, not the date window.

item.name: Delivery Person
item.description: Delivery-person task management. AUTH CAVEAT: only 'tasks/today' is scoped to the caller — every other endpoint here acts on any task id supplied, with no ownership check (see docs).

request.description: Today's assigned bookings + subscription deliveries for the authenticated delivery person. The ONLY delivery-person endpoint actually scoped to the caller's own id.
NOT scoped to the caller — any authenticated delivery person can view any task by id.
Hard-sets status to out_for_delivery (booking) / assigned (subscription) regardless of current status — no predecessor-state validation.
payment_collected.amount presence (not its value) flips payment_status to paid for booking tasks; omit it to leave payment_status unchanged.
Currently a stub server-side — location is not persisted; distance/ETA in the response are hardcoded placeholders, not computed from these coordinates.
Marks a batch of bookings and/or subscription tasks as delivered/completed. Per-item failures don't abort the rest of the batch.

Bookings only (not subscription tasks). WARNING: status:'failed' currently raises an invalid-enum error server-side ('failed_delivery' isn't a real Booking status) and aborts the ENTIRE batch with a 500 — avoid sending status:'failed' until fixed; use status:'delivered' or bulk_mark_done in the meantime.

item.name: Agent Dashboard, Leads & Commission
item.description: Agent/sub-agent/admin facing endpoints. Requires role 'agent' or 'sub_agent' in the JWT.

request.description: Summary stats + recent activity. Response shape varies by tier (admin/sub-agent/agent).

NOTE: every row includes a plaintext demo `password` field derived from the customer's name+mobile — flagged as a security concern in the docs, not a real account password, but worth knowing before logging/displaying this response.

Creates a Customer + User login attributed to the calling agent/sub-agent. Response envelope uses `status` (boolean), not `success` — different from most other agent endpoints. Password is auto-generated if omitted (returned in password_info).

Static dropdown data for policy/lead/customer forms. NOTE: 'health' still appears as an option in several dropdowns even though HealthInsurance was removed from the app — there is no endpoint to actually create a health policy.
Real DB-backed InsuranceCompany directory — distinct from the hardcoded static list in form_data.
Every authenticated agent/sub-agent sees ALL leads system-wide — no agent-scoping is applied (explicit in code comments).
Response envelope uses `status` (boolean), not `success`. Duplicate contact_number/email against ANY existing lead (not scoped to caller) is rejected with 422.
Sub-agent-tier CommissionPayout rows only, regardless of caller tier. NOTE: policy_number/customer_name are always 'N/A' in current code — a known gap, not a bug in this collection (see docs).
Aggregate earnings (total/paid/pending, this/last month) by policy_type. Computed differently for sub-agents (from LifeInsurance directly) vs. agents/admins (from CommissionPayout, unscoped).
